title: Boundary Dependency: How Much of Mumbai Indians’s Scoring Comes in Fours and Sixes?
dek: How much of Mumbai Indians' scoring comes in fours and sixes, and is a boundary-heavy innings a winning one? The data separates power from dependency.
excerpt: Since 2024 Mumbai Indians have taken more of their runs in boundaries than the league. Across the IPL, boundary-heavy innings win more often, but the reasons are not as simple as hitting harder.
author: CricField Editorial Desk
keyTakeaways: {{ev:bnd-t2}} of Mumbai Indians' runs since 2024 came in fours and sixes; the league figure is {{ev:bnd-l2}}.
IPL innings built on boundaries for 65% or more of their runs won {{ev:bnd-whigh}} of the time; under 55%, {{ev:bnd-wlow}}.
Across all seasons, {{ev:bnd-tall}} of Mumbai Indians' runs have come from boundaries.

sections.heading: Counting the Ropes
body: Boundary dependency is easy to talk about and rarely measured. For Mumbai Indians the measurement is simple: since 2024, {{ev:bnd-t2}} of their runs have come in fours and sixes off the bat, against {{ev:bnd-l2}} for the league as a whole.

Over their full history the figure is {{ev:bnd-tall}}. The season chart shows how far the whole league has moved towards boundary hitting, which is the backdrop any team-level comparison has to sit against.
On this measure their most boundary-reliant season was 2025, at {{ev:bnd-x-best-v}}, and their least boundary-reliant 2009, at {{ev:bnd-x-worst-v}}.

sections.heading: Do Boundaries Win Matches?
body: Across every IPL innings with a result, those that took 65% or more of their runs in boundaries won {{ev:bnd-whigh}} of the time, while those under 55% won {{ev:bnd-wlow}}.

Part of that link is cause and part is effect: an innings with many boundaries is usually a big total, and big totals win. A high boundary share also means fewer runs from running, which is exactly the skill that keeps an innings moving when boundaries dry up.

sections.heading: Dependency Versus Firepower
body: The tactical risk is not a high boundary share; it is the absence of a fallback. A side that relies on boundaries more than the league needs batters who can rotate strike on the days the ball is not coming onto the bat.
For MI, that means judging middle-order batters partly on singles and twos per ball, not only on sixes per innings.

sections.heading: The Conditions Caveat
body: Boundary share depends on where a side plays. Home grounds with short boundaries inflate it, and a season spent at big grounds deflates it, regardless of approach.

sections.heading: CricField Verdict: Power With a Plan B
body: Mumbai Indians should not fear boundary dependency; the league-wide data says boundary-heavy innings win. What they should guard against is a batting order with no way of scoring when the boundaries stop.
The measurable test is simple: runs from non-boundary balls per over in the middle overs, tracked alongside the boundary share.

methodology: Regulation innings only (super overs excluded). Run rates use all runs per legal ball times six. Every figure is generated from the CricField warehouse by scripts/editorial/engine. Boundary runs are fours and sixes off the bat. Win-rate bands use innings from matches with a result.
